Subject: Re: Questions on private deployment billing model

Hi Claire — thanks for the clear list. I’ve attached an updated SOW (Novaclinic_SOW_v2.pdf) and a support tiers spreadsheet (support_tiers.xlsx) that lays out the three options we discussed:

1) Upfront platform fee + standard support (default) — platform fee invoiced up-front, support billed annually.
2) Amortized platform fee (12 / 18 / 24 months) + reduced up-front — amortization appears on monthly invoices as a platform line item.
3) Minimal platform fee + SRE retainer (monthly) — pushes more into OPEX, reduces upfront CAPEX.

High-level notes: amortization requires a committed term (>=12 months) and a modest discount on platform fee; SRE retainers are scoped by response times and on-call coverage. I’ve asked Marissa to include concrete numbers in the next message — but to be explicit, we can construct an 18-month amortization that lowers cash outlay by ~45% in year 1 and pairs with a tiered SRE retainer.

Irene — flagging any compliance/licensing caveats for air-gapped installs.

Next steps: Marissa will send a pricing matrix. If this looks directionally correct, we can prepare a DocuSign SOW for signature and surface a 30-day pilot credit.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Novaclinic_SOW_v2.pdf, support_tiers.xlsx

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on private deployment billing model — pricing breakdown

Claire / team — attaching the pricing_breakdown.xlsx with three modeled scenarios (numbers are illustrative but accurate to our chassis):

Scenario A — Upfront: 250k platform fee (one-time), support T1 (12% of platform fee annually), no retainer.
Scenario B — Amortized 18m: 150k upfront platform, remaining 120k amortized over 18 months (~6.7k/mo), support T1 at 10% annually, 30k SRE retainer optional for monthly on-call/weekly ops reviews.
Scenario C — OPEX-forward: 50k platform upfront, 200k amortized + 60k annual SRE retainer (higher), includes 40 hours/month of dedicated SRE and SLA guarantee for patch windows.

Tradeoffs to call out for procurement and finance:
- Amortization reduces FY27 CAPEX but increases operating spend; supports predictable monthly accounting.
- SRE retainer compresses risk (we provide named SLA coverage), but counts as ongoing operational expense; we can offer step-down credits if NovaClinic self-manages certain on-call tasks.
- For air-gapped installs, additional one-time install fee and yearly escrow/licensing cost apply (listed in the spreadsheet).

If you prefer, we can present a blended proposal: amortize platform over 18 months AND provide a smaller SRE retainer (Scenario B hybrid). That reduces year-1 cash by ~60% vs. full upfront and gives 20 hours/month SRE coverage.

Ben — can you confirm whether we can extend a 10% loyalty discount if they commit to a 36-month support contract?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Pricing Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing_breakdown.xlsx

Evelyn / Marissa,

Thanks for the three scenarios — useful framing. A few follow-ups from procurement:
- NovaClinic would prefer to avoid large upfront CAPEX in FY27. The amortized 18m option (hybrid) is attractive.
- We need a clear definition of SRE retainer deliverables (on-call rota, escalation SLAs, 3rd-party patching windows). Can you codify that into an exhibit?
- We may ask for a one-time implementation discount tied to a 24-month commitment for support to reduce year-1 cash further.

Also, Claire asked if a 30-day pilot with a reduced scope (no full KV cache) is possible while we finalize commercials. If so, we want the pilot to start as soon as the SOW is countersigned.

Best,
